## Loading in the data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(glmnet)

train <- read_csv("data-train.csv")

# Calculate the four target statistics
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    m1 = R_moment_1,
    m2 = R_moment_2,
    m3 = R_moment_3,
    m4 = R_moment_4,

    C_moment_2 = m2 - m1^2,
    C_moment_3 = m3 - 3*m1*m2 + 2*m1^3,
    C_moment_4 = m4 - 4*m1*m3 + 6*m1^2*m2 - 3*m1^4,

    sd_R = sqrt(C_moment_2),
    skewness = C_moment_3 / sd_R^3,
    kurtosis = C_moment_4 / sd_R^4,
    ex_kurt = kurtosis - 3,
  )

# Only use the three input parameters as predictors
X <- train %>%
  select(Re, Fr, St)

# The four required outcomes
Y <- train %>%
  select(R_moment_1, sd_R, skewness, kurtosis)

# Check for Y
summary(Y)
```

## Model Fitting

```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(log_St = log(St))

pairwise <- paste0(
  "Re * Fr_invlogit + ",
  "Re * log_St + ",
  "Fr_invlogit * log_St"
)

models <- list(
  M1_linear = skewness ~ Re + Fr_invlogit + log_St,

  M2_pairwise = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise)
  ),

  M3_quadratic_only =
    skewness ~ Re + Fr_invlogit + log_St +
    I(Re^2) + I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2),

  M4_pairwise_S2 = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise, "+ I(log_St^2)")
  ),

  M5_pairwise_R2_S2 = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise,
          "+ I(Re^2) + I(log_St^2)")
  ),

  M6_pairwise_F2_S2 = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise,
          "+ I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)")
  ),

  M7_full_quadratic = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise,
          "+ I(Re^2) + I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)")
  ),

  M8_three_way =
    skewness ~ Re * Fr_invlogit * log_St,

  M9_three_way_selected_squares =
    skewness ~ Re * Fr_invlogit * log_St +
    I(Re^2) + I(log_St^2)
)
```


```{r}
# Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "LOOCV"
)

# Fit and compare all models
results <- lapply(names(models), function(nm) {
  fit <- caret::train(
    models[[nm]],
    data = train,
    method = "lm",
    trControl = ctrl,
    metric = "RMSE"
  )

  tibble(
    model = nm,
    RMSE = fit$results$RMSE[1],
    MAE = fit$results$MAE[1]
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

print(results)
```

```{r}
# Assumes `train` already exists (with skewness computed) from the earlier chunk.
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
 
train <- train %>%

models <- list(
  M1_linear          = mk("Re + Fr_invlogit + log_St"),
  M2_pairwise        = mk(pairwise),
  M3_quadratic_only  = mk("Re + Fr_invlogit + log_St + I(Re^2) + I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)"),
  M4_pairwise_S2     = mk(paste(pairwise, "+ I(log_St^2)")),
  M5_pairwise_R2_S2  = mk(paste(pairwise, "+ I(Re^2) + I(log_St^2)")),
  M6_pairwise_F2_S2  = mk(paste(pairwise, "+ I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)")),
  M7_full_quadratic  = mk(paste(pairwise, "+ I(Re^2) + I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)")),
  M8_three_way       = mk("Re * Fr_invlogit * log_St"),
  M9_three_way_sq    = mk("Re * Fr_invlogit * log_St + I(Re^2) + I(log_St^2)")
)
 
# LOOCV; keep the held-out predictions so we can also report raw-scale error
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "LOOCV", savePredictions = "final")
 
results <- lapply(names(models), function(nm) {
  fit <- caret::train(models[[nm]], data = train, method = "lm",
                      trControl = ctrl, metric = "RMSE")
  p <- fit$pred
  tibble(
    model    = nm,
    RMSE_log = fit$results$RMSE[1],
    MAE_log  = fit$results$MAE[1],
    RMSE_raw = sqrt(mean((exp(p$pred) - exp(p$obs))^2))  # back-transformed
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(RMSE_log)
 
print(results, n = Inf)
 
# Baselines for context (an intercept-only model gets about these)
cat("\nSD of log(skewness):", sd(train$log_skew), "\n")
cat("SD of raw skewness :", sd(train$skewness), "\n")
```

## adding some stuff to justify w EDA
```{r}
pairwise <- "Re * Fr_invlogit + Re * log_St + Fr_invlogit * log_St"
mk <- function(rhs) as.formula(paste("log_skew ~", rhs))
 
models <- list(
  # --- original set ---
  M1_linear          = mk("Re + Fr_invlogit + log_St"),
  M2_pairwise        = mk(pairwise),
  M3_quadratic_only  = mk("Re + Fr_invlogit + log_St + I(Re^2) + I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)"),
  M4_pairwise_S2     = mk(paste(pairwise, "+ I(log_St^2)")),
  M5_pairwise_R2_S2  = mk(paste(pairwise, "+ I(Re^2) + I(log_St^2)")),
  M6_pairwise_F2_S2  = mk(paste(pairwise, "+ I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)")),
  M7_full_quadratic  = mk(paste(pairwise, "+ I(Re^2) + I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)")),
  M8_three_way       = mk("Re * Fr_invlogit * log_St"),
  M9_three_way_sq    = mk("Re * Fr_invlogit * log_St + I(Re^2) + I(log_St^2)"),
 
  # --- new, motivated by the EDA plots: tiers set by Re x Fr (incl. squared terms), weak St effect ---
  # B: full (Re, Re^2) x (Fr, Fr^2) crossing + linear log St  (cell-means-like ceiling; one NA coef expected)
  B_ReFr_full        = mk("(Re + I(Re^2)) * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2)) + log_St"),
  # C: B + curvature in log St
  C_ReFr_full_S2     = mk("(Re + I(Re^2)) * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2)) + log_St + I(log_St^2)"),
  # D: Re linear only (no Re^2) crossed with Fr terms, + curved log St
  D_ReFr_noRe2_S2    = mk("Re * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2)) + log_St + I(log_St^2)"),
  # E: D + St slopes that differ by Re / Fr
  E_D_plus_St_inter  = mk("Re * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2)) + log_St + I(log_St^2) + Re:log_St + Fr_invlogit:log_St"),
  F_noSt = mk("(Re + I(Re^2)) * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2))")
)
 
# LOOCV; keep the held-out predictions so we can also report raw-scale error
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "LOOCV", savePredictions = "final")
 
small_St <- train$St == min(train$St)   # the St = 0.05 rows (where the outliers are)
 
results <- lapply(names(models), function(nm) {
  fit <- caret::train(models[[nm]], data = train, method = "lm",
                      trControl = ctrl, metric = "RMSE")
  p <- fit$pred
  keep <- !small_St[p$rowIndex]
  tibble(
    model        = nm,
    RMSE_log     = fit$results$RMSE[1],
    MAE_log      = fit$results$MAE[1],
    RMSE_log_no_smallSt = sqrt(mean((p$pred[keep] - p$obs[keep])^2)),  # diagnostic only
    RMSE_raw     = sqrt(mean((exp(p$pred) - exp(p$obs))^2))
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(RMSE_log)
 
print(results, n = Inf)
 
cat("\nSD of log(skewness):", sd(train$log_skew), "\n")
cat("SD of raw skewness :", sd(train$skewness), "\n")
```
C_ReFr_full_S2 (log(skewness) ~ (Re + I(Re^2)) * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2)) + log_St + I(log_St^2)) has lowest RMSE and MAE

```{r}
summary(model_C)
```

## Lasso/Variable Selection

```{r}
# Run AFTER skewness_loocv.R (needs `train` with Fr_invlogit, log_St, log_skew).
library(tidyverse)
library(glmnet)

# 0. Optional centering (reduces collinearity between x and x^2; helps the lasso).
#    If TRUE, remember to subtract these SAME training means from data-test.csv.
center <- FALSE
ctr <- c(Re = mean(train$Re), Fr = mean(train$Fr_invlogit), St = mean(train$log_St))
train_l <- train %>%
  mutate(Re_v = if (center) Re - ctr["Re"]           else Re,
         Fr_v = if (center) Fr_invlogit - ctr["Fr"]  else Fr_invlogit,
         St_v = if (center) log_St - ctr["St"]       else log_St)

# 1. BIG candidate pool: all pairwise products of Re, Re^2, Fr, Fr^2, logSt, logSt^2
#    (6 main effects + 15 products) plus the three-way Re:Fr:logSt term so that
#    M8/M9-type terms are covered too. 22 columns for 89 rows.
pool_formula <- log_skew ~ (Re_v + I(Re_v^2) + Fr_v + I(Fr_v^2) + St_v + I(St_v^2))^2 +
  Re_v:Fr_v:St_v

X <- model.matrix(pool_formula, data = train_l)[, -1]   # drop intercept column
y <- train_l$log_skew
n <- nrow(X)
cat("Candidate columns:", ncol(X), "\n")

# 2. LOOCV lasso / elastic net. glmnet standardizes columns internally.
#    alpha = 1 is the lasso; alpha < 1 mixes in ridge (better with correlated terms).
#    Explicit, wide lambda path so the CV optimum isn't cut off at either end.
set.seed(325)
alphas <- c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)
lam    <- 10^seq(0.5, -7, length.out = 150)
cv_fits <- lapply(alphas, function(a)
  cv.glmnet(X, y, alpha = a, lambda = lam, nfolds = n, foldid = seq_len(n),
            grouped = FALSE, type.measure = "mse"))

cmp <- tibble(
  alpha        = alphas,
  RMSE_log_min = sapply(cv_fits, function(f) sqrt(min(f$cvm))),   # LOOCV RMSE at best lambda
  lambda_min   = sapply(cv_fits, function(f) f$lambda.min),
  n_terms_min  = sapply(cv_fits, function(f) sum(coef(f, s = "lambda.min")[-1] != 0)),
  lambda_1se   = sapply(cv_fits, function(f) f$lambda.1se),
  n_terms_1se  = sapply(cv_fits, function(f) sum(coef(f, s = "lambda.1se")[-1] != 0))
)
print(cmp)   # compare RMSE_log_min with RMSE_log of the lm models (model C was ~0.22)

# 3. Look at which terms survive for the lasso (alpha = 1)
pick <- which(alphas == 1)
fit  <- cv_fits[[pick]]

show_coefs <- function(s) {
  b <- as.matrix(coef(fit, s = s))
  tibble(term = rownames(b), coef = b[, 1]) %>%
    filter(coef != 0, term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    arrange(desc(abs(coef)))
}
cat("\nTerms kept at lambda.min:\n");  print(show_coefs("lambda.min"), n = Inf)
cat("\nTerms kept at lambda.1se (sparser):\n"); print(show_coefs("lambda.1se"), n = Inf)

# 4. Post-lasso refit: plain lm on the selected terms (descriptive only; p-values after
#    selection are not valid, and its LOOCV would be optimistic).
sel <- show_coefs("lambda.1se")$term
Xdf <- as.data.frame(X[, sel, drop = FALSE]); names(Xdf) <- make.names(sel)
refit <- lm(y ~ ., data = Xdf)
print(summary(refit))
```

```{r}
cat(sprintf("%.6f", b[1]))

for (i in 2:length(b)) {
  cat(sprintf(" %+.6f * %s", b[i], names(b)[i]))
}
cat("\n")
```

## trying spline
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(splines)

train <- train %>% mutate(small_St = as.numeric(St == min(St)))   # the St = 0.05 rows

# Re and Fr have only 3 distinct values each, so a spline there would equal a quadratic.
# Keep the Re x Fr "cell" structure from model C and put the spline on log St only.
cells <- "(Re + I(Re^2)) * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2))"
mk <- function(rhs) as.formula(paste("log_skew ~", rhs))

spl_models <- list(
  C_poly         = mk(paste(cells, "+ log_St + I(log_St^2)")),              # reference
  S_ns3          = mk(paste(cells, "+ ns(log_St, df = 3)")),                # natural cubic, 3 df
  S_ns4          = mk(paste(cells, "+ ns(log_St, df = 4)")),
  S_ns5          = mk(paste(cells, "+ ns(log_St, df = 5)")),
  S_bs3          = mk(paste(cells, "+ bs(log_St, df = 3)")),                # cubic B-spline
  S_bs_knot0.1   = mk(paste(cells, "+ bs(log_St, knots = log(0.1), degree = 3)")),  # knot at St = 0.1
  S_ns3_small    = mk(paste(cells, "+ ns(log_St, df = 3) + small_St"))      # + indicator for St = 0.05
)

# NOTE: caret's formula interface builds the spline basis once on all rows (knots come from
# all data), then does LOOCV on the columns. The leakage is only the knot locations: negligible.
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "LOOCV", savePredictions = "final")

spl_results <- lapply(names(spl_models), function(nm) {
  fit <- caret::train(
    spl_models[[nm]],
    data = train,
    method = "lm",
    trControl = ctrl,
    metric = "RMSE"
  )

  p <- fit$pred
  keep <- train$small_St[p$rowIndex] == 0

  tibble(
    model               = nm,
    RMSE_log            = sqrt(mean((p$pred - p$obs)^2)),
    MAE_log             = mean(abs(p$pred - p$obs)),
    RMSE_log_no_smallSt = sqrt(mean((p$pred[keep] - p$obs[keep])^2)),
    MAE_log_no_smallSt  = mean(abs(p$pred[keep] - p$obs[keep])),
    RMSE_raw            = sqrt(mean((exp(p$pred) - exp(p$obs))^2)),
    MAE_raw             = mean(abs(exp(p$pred) - exp(p$obs)))
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(RMSE_log)

print(spl_results, n = Inf)

# ---- Fitted curves per Re x Fr cell on top of the data (like your first EDA plot) ----
best_spline <- "S_ns3"                            # change to whichever spline you want to show
fit_s <- lm(spl_models[[best_spline]], data = train)

grid <- train %>%
  distinct(Re, Fr, Fr_invlogit) %>%
  crossing(St = sort(unique(c(train$St, seq(0.05, 3, length.out = 120))))) %>%
  mutate(log_St = log(St), small_St = 0)
grid$log_skew_hat <- predict(fit_s, newdata = grid)

p <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = train, aes(log_St, log_skew, color = factor(Re), shape = factor(Fr))) +
  geom_line(data = grid, aes(log_St, log_skew_hat, color = factor(Re),
                             linetype = factor(Fr), group = interaction(Re, Fr))) +
  labs(x = "log(St)", y = "log(skewness)", color = "Re", shape = "Fr", linetype = "Fr",
       title = paste("Fitted cell curves:", best_spline))
print(p)
ggsave("spline_fit_by_cell.png", p, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 200)

# ---- The St effect itself (same shape in every cell, since the model is additive in St) ----
effect <- grid %>% filter(Re == 224, Fr == 0.3) %>%
  mutate(effect_vs_St1 = log_skew_hat - log_skew_hat[which.min(abs(St - 1))])
p2 <- ggplot(effect, aes(St, effect_vs_St1)) + geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + scale_x_log10() +
  labs(y = "change in log(skewness) relative to St = 1",
       title = "Estimated St effect (same in every Re/Fr cell)")
print(p2)
ggsave("spline_St_effect.png", p2, width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 200)
```

# box cox
```{r}

library(MASS)

# Original response must be strictly positive
stopifnot(all(train$skewness > 0, na.rm = TRUE))

# Your original model structure
formula_bc <- skewness ~
  (Re + I(Re^2)) * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2)) +
  log_St + I(log_St^2)

# Estimate optimal Box-Cox lambda
bc <- boxcox(
  formula_bc,
  data = train,
  lambda = seq(-2, 2, by = 0.05),
  plotit = TRUE
)

lambda_hat <- bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]
cat("Optimal lambda:", lambda_hat, "\n")

# Transform the response using the estimated lambda
lambda <- lambda_hat

train$skewness_bc <- if (abs(lambda) < 1e-6) {
  log(train$skewness)
} else {
  (train$skewness^lambda - 1) / lambda
}

# Fit the transformed-response model
C_ReFr_full_S2_BC <- lm(
  skewness_bc ~
    (Re + I(Re^2)) * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2)) +
    log_St + I(log_St^2),
  data = train
)

summary(C_ReFr_full_S2_BC)

```

LOOCV
```{r}


library(MASS)

# Original model structure
formula_bc <- skewness ~
  (Re + I(Re^2)) * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2)) +
  log_St + I(log_St^2)

# LOOCV
n <- nrow(train)
predictions <- rep(NA_real_, n)
actual_bc <- rep(NA_real_, n)
lambdas <- rep(NA_real_, n)

for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  train_fold <- train[-i, ]
  test_fold  <- train[i, , drop = FALSE]

  # Estimate lambda using only the training fold
  bc <- boxcox(
    formula_bc,
    data = train_fold,
    lambda = seq(-2, 2, by = 0.05),
    plotit = FALSE
  )

  lambda_i <- bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]
  lambdas[i] <- lambda_i

  # Transform training response
  y <- train_fold$skewness

  train_fold$skewness_bc <- if (abs(lambda_i) < 1e-6) {
    log(y)
  } else {
    (y^lambda_i - 1) / lambda_i
  }

  # Fit model on transformed response
  fit <- lm(
    skewness_bc ~
      (Re + I(Re^2)) * (Fr_invlogit + I(Fr_invlogit^2)) +
      log_St + I(log_St^2),
    data = train_fold
  )

  # Predict held-out observation on transformed scale
  predictions[i] <- predict(fit, newdata = test_fold)

  # Transform held-out actual using the same fold-specific lambda
  y_test <- test_fold$skewness

  actual_bc[i] <- if (abs(lambda_i) < 1e-6) {
    log(y_test)
  } else {
    (y_test^lambda_i - 1) / lambda_i
  }
}

# Evaluate on Box-Cox-transformed skewness scale
valid <- is.finite(predictions) & is.finite(actual_bc)

RMSE_bc <- sqrt(mean(
  (actual_bc[valid] - predictions[valid])^2
))

MAE_bc <- mean(
  abs(actual_bc[valid] - predictions[valid])
)

cat("Valid folds:", sum(valid), "/", n, "\n")
cat("LOOCV RMSE (Box-Cox scale):", RMSE_bc, "\n")
cat("LOOCV MAE (Box-Cox scale):", MAE_bc, "\n")
cat("Mean fold lambda:", mean(lambdas, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("SD fold lambda:", sd(lambdas, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")


```
